module_description: How the IMS issues the three statutory aviation warning products: SIGMET and AIRMET for en-route hazards across the FIR, and AD WRNG / WS WRNG for hazards at the aerodrome. Focuses on ICAO Annex 3 thresholds, the IMS operational criteria layered on top of them, and the message syntax — what to write, when to write it, and when to coordinate one product with another.
competencies: Distinguish SIGMET, AIRMET, and aerodrome warnings by phenomenon, intensity threshold, and area of responsibility
Construct a syntactically valid SIGMET or AIRMET message including WMO header, validity, meteorological part, and lat/lon coordinates
Apply ICAO Annex 3 validity, lead-time, and cancellation rules to SIGMET and AIRMET issuance
Apply IMS-specific AD WRNG criteria for thunderstorms, low visibility, low cloud base, strong winds, and frost
Issue a wind-shear warning based on forecast, observation, or pilot report, including low-level jet conditions
Coordinate AD WRNG with SIGMET / AIRMET so the FIR-wide and aerodrome-local products stay consistent

lessons.lesson_title: The Aviation Warning Framework & SIGMET Phenomena
learning_objectives: Place SIGMET, AIRMET, and aerodrome warnings within the ICAO Annex 3 service hierarchy (MWO vs AFO; FIR vs aerodrome)
List the SIGMET phenomena and the severity qualifier required to trigger each (OBSC/EMBD/FRQ/SQL TS, SEV TURB, SEV ICE, SEV MTW, HVY DS/SS, VA, RDOACT)
Distinguish the three SIGMET subtypes (WS, WV, WC) and the data-type designator that identifies each
Decide whether a given observation/forecast triggers a SIGMET or stays below threshold
visual_elements_needed: Hierarchy diagram: WAFC → MWO (SIGMET/AIRMET) → AFO (TAF/AD WRNG), with the product issued at each tier
Decision-tree-style diagram mapping each SIGMET phenomenon to the qualifier required to trigger the message

learning_objectives: Decode every field of a SIGMET WMO header (T1T2A1A2ii CCCC YYGGgg)
Construct the first line of a SIGMET (FIR/MWO indicators, sequential number, validity period)
Write lat/lon coordinates in the ICAO Annex 3 format including the space-hyphen-space polygon convention
Issue a SIGMET cancellation message with the correct sequential numbering and validity reference
Apply the 4-hour validity ceiling, the 4-hour pre-occurrence lead-time limit, and the one-phenomenon-per-message rule
visual_elements_needed: Annotated SIGMET message with each field of the WMO header and first line called out by colour
Worked example showing an original SIGMET and its cancellation message side-by-side

learning_objectives: Apply the AIRMET scope rule (below FL100, en-route, not already covered by an existing low-level forecast)
Identify the AIRMET phenomenon list (ISOL/OCNL TS, MOD ICE, MOD TURB/MTW, sustained SFC wind ≥30 kt, ceiling <1000 ft, vis <5 km, extensive mountain obscuration)
Differentiate the spatial-coverage qualifiers ISOL (<50%), OCNL (50–75%), and FRQ (>75%)
Choose between issuing a SIGMET, an AIRMET, or no message at all given a forecast scenario near threshold
visual_elements_needed: Side-by-side table of AIRMET vs SIGMET thresholds for each shared phenomenon
Spatial-coverage diagram showing the ISOL/OCNL/FRQ percentage bands over a FIR outline

learning_objectives: Apply the IMS AD WRNG thresholds for TS/CB (within 16 km of runway centre), visibility (<5000 m), ceiling (BKN/OVC ≤1500 ft), surface wind (>20 kt mean / >30 kt gust), and severe hail (≥2 cm)
Construct a valid AD WRNG message and the equivalent WS WRNG message, including the phenomenon code (TS, GR, HVY SN, FZRA, SFC WSPD, SQ, FROST, TSUNAMI, VA, free text)
Issue a WS WRNG based on forecaster judgement (FCST), observation (OBS — AMDAR/sonde/pilot), or aircraft report (REP AT), including the low-level-jet criterion (peak ≥30 kt below 2000 ft AGL)
Coordinate AD WRNG issuance with SIGMET / AIRMET so the FIR-wide and aerodrome-local products stay consistent — and recognise the cases where coordination is not required (e.g. WS WRNG for LLJ)
visual_elements_needed: Annotated AD WRNG and WS WRNG messages with each field called out
Coordination decision matrix: phenomenon at aerodrome vs FIR-wide → which products to issue
Cross-section diagram of a low-level jet over the runway, showing surface vs 500 m and the 15 kt / 30 kt shear thresholds

module_quiz.description: End-of-module summative assessment covering SIGMET, AIRMET, and aerodrome/wind-shear warning issuance against ICAO Annex 3 and IMS operational criteria.
module_quiz.note: V2 meteorology expansion grew the per-lesson question pool to 32 (8 per lesson).
